How to Execute the Refund Workflow

Responsible Teams and Roles
Claims Specialists, Customer Support Leads, Operations Manager

Refund Workflow Runbook

Purpose
This runbook explains the refund workflow for reviewing, approving, executing, and documenting customer refunds for e-commerce orders. It is used when a customer requests a refund, when Operations initiates a refund after a fulfillment failure, or when Claims must resolve a payment-related issue. The objective is to deliver a fair outcome quickly while maintaining financial controls and a complete audit trail.

When to Use
Use this runbook for full refunds, partial refunds, duplicate-charge corrections, non-delivery cases, damage claims approved for monetary resolution, and service recovery situations where policy supports a refund.

Responsible Roles
Primary owner: Claims Specialist or assigned Customer Support agent.
Approver: Team Lead for refunds above the frontline threshold or when the case is routed through Tier 2 escalation.
Secondary approver: Operations Manager for refunds above $500 or for exceptions outside policy.

Procedure
Step 1: Confirm the order number, customer identity, payment status, and refund request reason.
Step 2: Review order history, shipment status, prior case notes, and any previous concessions on the account.
Step 3: Check the refund reason against the current refund policy and any temporary campaign exceptions.
Step 4: Verify whether the issue qualifies for full refund, partial refund, replacement, store credit, or denial.
Step 5: If the refund amount is within your approval authority, prepare the refund summary and proceed. If it exceeds your authority, escalate with a concise note that includes order value, requested amount, root cause, and evidence.
Step 6: Confirm that no active chargeback, duplicate refund, or payment dispute is already in process.
Step 7: Execute the refund in the payment platform using the correct reason code and amount, including tax and shipping treatment where applicable.
Step 8: Record the refund transaction reference, approval level, and supporting rationale in the case system.
Step 9: Send the customer the approved communication template explaining amount, timing, and any next steps.
Step 10: Add follow-up tasks if Finance review, claim recovery, or root-cause analysis is required.

Approval Requirements
Refunds up to $100 may be approved by authorized frontline agents when policy is clear.
Refunds from $100.01 to $500 require team-lead approval.
Refunds above $500 require Operations Manager approval.
Any suspected fraud, repeat abuse pattern, or high-risk concession requires Risk or Claims review regardless of amount.

Quality Checks
Verify that the refunded amount matches the approved resolution.
Ensure the customer communication reflects full or partial refund correctly.
Confirm the case record includes who approved the refund and why.

Escalation Guidance
Escalate immediately if the case involves payment processor failure, repeated concessions, VIP executive handling, or conflicting order data across systems.

Completion Criteria
The runbook is complete when the refund is executed or denied, the customer has been informed, and the case record contains the audit trail needed for later review.
